title: Exploring Ideas Through Talk
keyIdea: Talk helps you think. Say "maybe" and "what if?" to get lots of ideas, not just one. Give a reason with "because" and a clue you can see. Test a what-if to find out. Try new words out loud, and add to a friend's idea with "yes, and".

kid: Talk can help you think. When you do not know, say maybe. Maybe the sun dried the puddle. Maybe it sank into the mud. Think of lots of ideas, not just one.
Say why with because. Use a clue you can see. The coat is wet because it is raining.
Ask what if. What if we put the ice in the freezer? Then try it and see.
Try new words when you talk. A big ball can be enormous. When a friend has an idea, say yes, and add to it.
adult: This topic is exploratory talk: thinking out loud before settling on an answer. Children wonder about possibilities, give reasons, imagine what might happen, and try out new words they have heard. The English national curriculum asks pupils to use spoken language to develop understanding through speculating, hypothesising, imagining and exploring ideas, and to build vocabulary through talk.

The lab gives each move its own job. Several maybes go into a thinking cloud before any answer is chosen. A reason must use a clue in the picture. A what-if is tested with an ice cube in the sun, the shade and a freezer. New words are matched to pictures, and a den grows only when a reply adds to a friend's idea.

Common mistakes: stopping at the first idea or saying I don't know; giving a reason that just repeats the question, such as the coat is wet because it is wet; giving a reason that is not a clue at all; saying no to a friend's idea instead of building on it; and hearing a new word without ever saying it yourself.

Wonder aloud together on walks and at bath time. Ask what do you think and why, and accept several answers before testing one. Use story words in daily talk, and praise a child who adds to someone else's idea.

familyTip: At bath time, ask "What if we put this toy in the water?" Let your child give two maybes, each with a because. Then drop it in and talk about what really happened.

practice.prompt: The puddle is gone. Pip says, "Maybe the sun dried it." What should Pip do next?
practice.hint: Think of the thinking cloud. How many maybes did Pip get?
practice.explain: One idea is a start. More maybes, like the soil or a dog, help find the best one.

practice.prompt: Ava has {n} ideas for the den. Leo says "Yes, and we can add a torch!" How many ideas now?
practice.hint: Did Leo take an idea away, or add one?
practice.explain: Yes, and adds a new idea, so {n} ideas become {=n+1}. Saying no would add none.

practice.prompt: Why is Tom's coat wet? Which answer gives a reason?
practice.hint: A reason says why. Which one uses a clue?
practice.explain: Rain is a clue that explains the wet coat. Saying it is wet again does not say why.

practice.prompt: Pip puts an ice cube in the freezer for {n} minutes. What happens?
practice.hint: Think of the ice test. Is the freezer warm or cold?
practice.explain: The freezer is colder than ice needs to stay solid, so after {n} minutes it is still ice.

pool.hint: Which words open up new ideas?
pool.explain: Maybe and what if invite new ideas. No and stop end the thinking.

pool.prompt: Why did the tower fall? Look: a dog is wagging its tail by the blocks.
choices: Because the dog's tail hit it
pool.hint: Use the clue you can see.
pool.explain: The wagging tail is the clue. Red is not a reason, and fell down just says it again.

pool.prompt: Which new word means very, very big?
pool.hint: Think of the huge orange ball.
pool.explain: Enormous means very, very big. Tiny means very small and soggy means wet and soft.

pool.prompt: Mia says, "Let's build a boat." What adds to her idea?
choices: Yes, and it can have a sail!
pool.hint: Which answer makes the boat idea bigger?
pool.explain: A sail adds to Mia's boat. No stops the idea, and cake is not about the boat.

pool.prompt: You put {n} ice cubes in the hot sun. What do you think will happen?
pool.hint: In the ice test, what did the sun do?
pool.explain: The sun warms the {n} ice cubes, so they melt into water.

pool.prompt: Leo thinks of {n} maybes for where the snowman went. Is that good thinking?
choices: No, you should say I don't know
pool.hint: Did more maybes help Pip with the puddle?
pool.explain: {n} maybes give Leo more to talk about and test, so he can pick the best one.

pool.prompt: Gran reads the word soggy in a story. How can you make it your word?
choices: Say it when you talk: my bread is soggy!
pool.hint: What helps a new word stick in your head?
pool.explain: Saying a new word out loud, in your own talk, helps you keep it.

pool.prompt: Why is the ice cream dripping? Which answer gives a reason?
pool.hint: Which answer says why, using a clue?
pool.explain: The hot sun melts the ice cream. The other answers do not say why it drips.

visual.caption: Does it help ideas grow, or stop them? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: give Pip lots of maybes, pick a because from a clue, test what-ifs with an ice cube, try new words and grow a friend's idea.
